decisions.summary: Feature 251's seeded harness reused as it stands (prepare, run_seeded.sh, R5 weight arithmetic); the candidate's agent-file edit is made in the clone so the worktree copy carries it; a NOT ADOPTED candidate is reverted before the next batch.
decisions.why: FR-001 names 251's seeded.py as the acceptance test and says a failing candidate leaves the agent as it was; this is how, not what.

decisions.summary: source-applicability's two cases are picked by seeded.py catalog from its 26 recorded runs, one with a NOT-APPLICABLE or MISSING verdict and one clean; batches run three at a time with run count and rough weight stated before launch.
decisions.why: FR-002 asks for two seeded cases and leaves the selection open; the pre-launch statement is FR-001's own instruction. Both counts (26 runs, 123 runs) re-run clean from scripts/_agent_census.py --until 2026-09-19, the command recorded under census.* in 251's measurements.json.

decisions.summary: scripts/_source_entries.py parses SOURCES.html plus the citations pages by importing _quote_verbatim.footnotes/assertions; the contract gains a 'step 0'.
decisions.why: FR-002 specifies exactly this output (citation line, both write-ups, Used for:, the citing footnotes with assertions) and the contract instruction. Both imported helpers exist.

decisions.summary: _record_prepass.py --section gains --text (visible text plus numbered HTML source lines after the candidate list); quote-verbatim --notes already carries passage and assertion.
decisions.why: FR-003 asks for the section's visible text and its HTML source lines, and states quote-verbatim already carries its part.

decisions.summary: One identical sentence placed under each of the seven contracts' opening paragraph, tested on the twin's verify-250-cr and verify-clean cases against R7's runs and the recorded runs.
decisions.why: FR-004 asks for one instruction in the same words in exactly those seven files, tested on two later spec-fidelity rounds on the twin.

decisions.summary: scripts/_source_pages.py promoted from 253's measure/fetch_text.py with a pointer|file|state manifest; the reader greps then reads around hits; URLs taken from each recorded prompt by the session, not by a model.
decisions.why: FR-006 asks for a no-model page saver and the grep-then-read contract, judged on R5's three cases.

decisions.summary: The fixed-context probes run on Haiku from /diagram, varying one suspect at a time: the tool list, a scratch copy of the repository with CLAUDE.md removed, the appended system prompt present or absent.
decisions.why: FR-007 asks for probe runs on the cheapest model dispatched inside this repository, with and without each suspect, and a recorded breakdown.

decisions.summary: The session memory index is probed with and without ONLY IF the harness allows pointing at a scratch copy of the memory directory; otherwise its size is reported from its character count and the per-token ratio measured on the other probes.
decisions.why: FR-007 requires probe runs that MEASURE what each suspect adds to a subagent's first-turn input, the memory index named as one of four, and the request's finding this feature exists to close is that what fills the 47-67 k fixed context 'was not established'. A character count times a ratio estimates a document's size; it does not establish what the index adds to a dispatch, which is the one thing the finding says is unknown. Nor is the measurement impossible: the plan's own CLAUDE.md leg already probes from a scratch copy of the repository, and a scratch copy has its own (empty) project memory directory, so the paired probe (scratch copy with CLAUDE.md present, no memory index) against /diagram (CLAUDE.md present, memory index present) IS the measured delta on instruments the plan already builds. A carve-out written in advance against an untested harness limitation is a session excusing itself from a measurement before it has tried to take one. Remove the fallback: probe the memory index like the other three suspects, and if it genuinely proves impossible after the attempt, that is a measured obstacle to put to the GM, not a pre-authorized substitution.

decisions.summary: Memory index lines shortened to a hook of at most 120 characters, every entry kept; a tool an agent's recorded runs never called (R9's per-tool counts) removed from its tools: line.
decisions.why: FR-007 permits exactly two trims in these terms, and 'every entry kept, lines shortened' is honored. Note for the session, not a fidelity finding: 'never called in the recorded runs' is weaker than FR-007's 'a tool the check never calls' - a tool the contract itself tells the agent to use is not removable on a sample of runs.

decisions.summary: scripts/_review_facts.py runs in one call the measurements settlement-review.md's Tooling section already names and prints them together; two cases picked by seeded.py catalog from the smallest of the 123 recorded runs.
decisions.why: FR-005 asks for that script and two seeded runs; both named contract sections exist in the file.

decisions.summary: The Validated examples section moves to .claude/agents/settlement-review-examples.md, and the move is DROPPED if test_agent_models.py cannot tell that file from an agent without changing what it asserts.
decisions.why: FR-005 states the move as part of the candidate: the contract's Validated examples section MOVES to a file the agent opens only when a finding of that kind is in doubt, and FR-001 decides adoption by measured findings-and-weight, not by a test's convenience. The plan's stated ground is also factually wrong: test_agent_models.py derives its roster from AGENTS.glob('*.md'), and frontmatter() asserts 'no YAML frontmatter' on a file that carries none, so a frontmatter-less examples file in .claude/agents/ fails the test - the condition is not a contingency, it fires. That makes the carve-out an unconditional dropping of a spec requirement dressed as an if. It is also plainly avoidable: nothing in the request or the spec puts the examples file in .claude/agents/, so the section can move to any path outside the agents directory (docs/, or a skill path) with the test untouched, as FR-008 requires. Remove the condition and name a location that does not collide with the roster.

decisions.summary: T01 source-entries, T02 scoped text, T03 batching line, T04 source-pages, T05 probes and trims, T06 review-facts, T07 record, T08 gates; each of T01-T06 ends with its batch scored and the candidate ADOPTED or NOT ADOPTED.
decisions.why: The spec's own assumption sets this cheapest-first order with settlement-review last, and SC-002 requires the per-candidate verdict.

decisions.summary: No engine code; scripts, agents, the skill Makefile (GUARD_EDIT_OK with a reason), tests/tooling and docs route DIRECT.
decisions.why: The spec's Summary states the DIRECT route and SC-004 requires nothing under l7r/ or pool/ to change.
